subject: Procurement path clarification — prepay, card, and marketplace options
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Patel <alex.patel@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap from today — procurement path & next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for joining the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with your procurement rules: 

- Summary: Your engineering team liked the latency profile on the 8k LLM and the integration path looks straightforward. Primary commercial blockers appear to be: (1) whether this can go through your AWS Marketplace vs direct Redwood invoice, and (2) your finance policy around POs vs card/prepay.

- From our side: we can accept card, invoice (net-30/60), or Marketplace (AWS/GCP). We can also do a prepay/committed arrangement for reserved capacity if that helps unblock approvals.

- Questions for procurement:
  1) Does FinServ require a formal PO for vendors under $250k/yr, or is an exception possible for SaaS/invoice?
  2) Is Marketplace preferred (so charges appear on cloud bill) or do you need Redwood to be in your vendor master first?
  3) Any prepay constraints (e.g., finance requires vendor registration + proof of insurance before prepay)?

Next steps I propose: I can pull together a short commercial one-pager and a draft SOW + quote for the committed-reserved option (prepay) and a card/credit option for immediate pilots. If procurement confirms they cannot issue a PO to a non-registered vendor, we can start vendor onboarding in parallel.

I've attached a pricing quote and a standard SOW template for your review. Can you loop in whoever owns vendor onboarding or confirm whether Procurement (procure@finservcorp.com) should be the point of contact?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0193

Attachments: redwood-pricing-quote-2026-01-12.xlsx, redwood-sow-template.pdf
From: Alex Patel <alex.patel@finservcorp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@finservcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap from today — procurement path & next steps

Thanks Jasmine — good summary. Quick answers from my side and forwarding to procurement for details.

- On POs: Our standard is to issue POs for any vendor spend > $50k annually. For smaller pilots (< $50k) we often allow credit card or a short-term invoice, but it requires a spend approval from my manager + a vendor form.
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace purchases where available because it simplifies cloud billing. BUT our cloud team only approves marketplace purchases for vendors that are in their approved partner list. Becoming an approved marketplace seller can take 3–6 weeks.
- Prepay: Procurement usually avoids large prepayments unless there's a contract and evidence of insurance/W9/vendor registration. Short prepaid pilots (~1 month) are sometimes OK with a PO + vendor onboarding.

Forwarding to Procurement for the definitive path — @procure, can you confirm if you can issue a one-time PO for a pilot or if we need vendor registration first? Also attaching the vendor form we typically ask new vendors to fill out.

—Alex
Director, Engineering | FinServ Corp
alex.patel@finservcorp.com

On Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 09:18 AM Procurement Team <procure@finservcorp.com> wrote:
> Please see attached vendor form. Procurement will review and advise on PO/exceptions.

Attachments: finserv-vendor-form.pdf
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Alex Patel <alex.patel@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap from today — procurement path & next steps

Alex / Jasmine — quick suggestion from our side to reduce friction: 

Option A (fastest pilot): Card or Stripe charge for a 30-day pilot (under $10k) — no PO required; we can generate an invoice after the fact if needed. This is the fastest for a dev/proof-of-concept.

Option B (preferred for production): Vendor onboarding + PO or invoice (net-30). We can prepare a short SOW that limits initial committed spend to $40k so it sits under your $50k PO threshold if you prefer a PO path. If Procurement requires prepay, we can do a 50% prepay on sign and 50% on go-live.

Option C (marketplace): We can start the marketplace onboarding but that will likely push timelines ~4–6 weeks. If marketplace is required, we recommend starting vendor/master onboarding now while doing a short card-based pilot to keep momentum.

I uploaded an updated quote that reflects a 3-month pilot and a conservative reserved commit (see attached). If Proc needs a vendor form filled by Redwood, Marcus can take point to complete vendor paperwork & supply COI/W9 quickly.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | (646) 555-0112

Attachments: redwood-pricing-quote-2026-01-12.xlsx
From: Procurement Team <procure@finservcorp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Alex Patel <alex.patel@finservcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap from today — procurement path & next steps

Hello Jasmine and team,

Thanks for the details and the attachments. A few notes from procurement after an internal review: 

1) Vendor onboarding: We require the vendor form completed and a W9 + proof of insurance (COI) for any invoice/PO. We received finserv-vendor-form.pdf from Alex — please complete and return.
2) PO exceptions: We can issue a one-time PO for a pilot up to $50k, provided the vendor is registered or the PO is contingent on onboarding completion. If Redwood prefers to avoid onboarding overhead, we can accept card payment for pilots under $10k (suitable for initial dev work).
3) Prepay: Procurement does not typically authorize >30-day prepayments without Finance sign-off. A 50% prepay for reserved capacity is possible if you provide a contract and COI; Finance will need to see vendor registration progress.
4) Marketplace: We can purchase via AWS Marketplace, but only after Redwood is a listed partner. That process is separate and will take several weeks. If you can provide a short partner onboarding checklist, we can start that in parallel.

Please have Marcus Lin (or your vendor admin) fill the vendor form and attach W9/COI. If you want us to proceed with a PO contingent on onboarding, indicate that in your reply and we will start the internal approvals.

Regards,
Procurement Team
FinServ Corp
procure@finservcorp.com

Attachments requested: finserv-vendor-form.pdf (filled), W9, COI
